speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a psychiatric condition and a new movement disorder; to help me evaluate this, can you describe what these new movements look like and when they first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful information; given your recent diagnosis of schizophrenia and the initiation of risperidone two months ago, could you describe specifically what these new movements look like, such as stiffness, tremors, or repetitive motions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for describing your symptoms; these signs of akathisia—inability to remain still, fidgeting, and leg crossing—are a common side effect of your risperidone. To confirm this, I need to know if you have experienced any muscle stiffness, tremors, or swallowing difficulties?

REQUEST TEST: Clinical Exam (Neurological & Extrapyramidal Signs)
REQUEST IMAGES: None

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Neurological Examination reveals intact cranial nerves, normal tone and strength in all extremities, no involuntary movements noted (specifically no muscle stiffness or tremors), intact sensory function, normal coordination, and normal gait; however, the patient exhibits inability to sit still with frequent pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia secondary to Risperidone therapy.

The neurological exam rules out Parkinsonism or other movement disorders, and the symptoms of inner restlessness with an inability to sit still are classic for akathisia. Would you like to discuss management strategies or request a follow-up plan for symptom relief?
